name: Data Table
tagline: A sortable, filterable table over any Dataverse view, with inline editing, pinned columns and a New button.

limitations: Paging is inert. The demo harness puts every fixture row on a single page and reports hasNextPage and hasPreviousPage as false, so Next and Previous render disabled and loadNextPage() only re-renders the same rows. The page size property does nothing either, because the harness’s setPageSize() is an empty function.

Sorting a column moves the sort arrow but does not reorder the rows. The control writes into dataset.sorting and calls refresh(), which is what a real view needs because sorting is applied server-side across every page — but the harness rebuilds the dataset with an empty sorting array on each render and discards the request. Multi-column sort is off by default and there is nothing to be gained by turning it on here: it appends a second column to dataset.sorting rather than replacing the first, so the harness discards a list of two exactly as it discards a list of one.

Clicking a row calls dataset.openDatasetItem(). There is no form behind this origin to open, so the event log under the demo names the record that would have opened instead. The openedRecordId output still updates, so the value a form would react to is visible.

Rows tick and untick, but dataset.setSelectedRecordIds() does not survive a re-render for the same reason sorting does not. What you see is the control’s own copy of the selection. On a model-driven form that same call is what tells the command bar which records the ribbon acts on.

Typing in a filter box narrows nothing here, and that is structural rather than a gap in effort. Filtering is applied by the server across every page — the control calls dataset.filtering.setFilter() and then refresh() — and there is no server behind this origin. What the demo does show is the half worth seeing: the filter row renders per column type, so you can watch which columns get a box and which deliberately do not. The event log records the refresh() each filter sends; the expression a real view would have been filtered by stays inside the control.

Export CSV is on in the Filtering and export preset and builds a real file from the records on the page. The control hands it to navigation.openFile, as it does on a form; the demo cannot save a file from inside its sandbox, so the event log under the demo offers it as a Download. What it cannot show is the choice 0.6.0 added: with Export scope set to the whole view the control walks the pages and reassembles them, and this harness has a single page and an inert pager, so both settings collect the same 24 rows and finish at once. On a real view that setting is the difference between the page you are looking at and up to ten thousand rows fetched a page at a time, which is why it ships with a progress counter and a Cancel.

Inline editing works here, and the write is real — against the demo's stand-in Dataverse. The harness carries the write half of a dataset record (setValue, save, isEditable), so an edit commits, survives the next render and the table shows it, but nothing leaves the browser: Reset or a reload puts the fixture back as authored. Account number is marked read-only in the fixture on purpose, so you can see the half that matters — the control asks the platform whether each cell is writable, per column and per record, and renders a refused one as plain text rather than offering an editor it would then have to take back.

A refused write still cannot be demonstrated. The harness’s save() always succeeds, so the rollback never runs — on a real form a write the user has no privilege for is rejected, the cell returns to its old value, and the reason is named underneath it. That path is the reason this control catches at all, and the demo is the one place you cannot see it.

Two 0.4.0 features are absent here rather than mocked: choice cells stay read-only, and choice columns keep the dash in the filter row. Both need the column's option set from utils.getEntityMetadata, and the demo's metadata carries none. Status in this fixture is a label string, where a real view hands over an integer — the dev rig in this repository carries the platform's shapes; the hub's fixture format cannot. The date filter box does render, and narrows nothing for the reason every other filter narrows nothing. The third, the New button, is drawn in the Inline editing preset, where Allow adding rows is on: it asks navigation.openForm for the table's quick create form, and with no form behind the demo the event log names the form that would have opened and no row is added.

Pinned columns are the one thing on this page that is not simulated at all — pinning is layout, so it needs no server and no dataset call, and what the Pinned columns preset shows is exactly what a form shows. A pinned column is only visible once there is something to scroll, so the fixture carries eight columns: pinned, the table asks for 940px, which is wider than this page gives it at any size. Switch to the Pinned columns preset and drag the scrollbar under the rows — Account name stays at the left edge, Modified on at the right, and everything between them passes behind. The one thing to try deliberately is the phone preview: below about 440px the pinned pair would leave nothing to scroll between them, so the control unpins itself rather than trap you, and that clamp is real behaviour rather than a demo shortcut.

Grouping runs here and its numbers are right, but by the browser route — the one a canvas app gets. The demo's stand-in Dataverse does not answer FetchXML, so the server aggregate over the whole view is refused and the control groups the rows it has loaded instead. The caption under the table says which route answered. Here that costs nothing, because the fixture is a single page: "the 24 records loaded so far" happens to be every record there is, so the counts and the summed revenue are the same numbers a server would have returned. On a view of four thousand rows that caption is the whole difference between a total and a page total. Expanding is the half that cannot work here. The chevron opens, the member rows appear and the pager comes back scoped to the group — but the rows underneath are every row in the fixture, because expanding a group is a filter rather than a scroll: it calls dataset.filtering.setFilter() and refresh(), the same pair the filter row calls, and the harness discards both for the same reason. Group by Owner or City. Status stays one blank group on purpose: the fixture carries the label "Active" where a real view hands over the integer behind it, and a Choice is grouped on the integer.

Primary contact is a lookup to contact, and editing it works against the demo's stand-in Dataverse by the same route as on a form. In the Inline editing preset, click a contact: Choose… opens a lookup dialog over the demo's contacts (utils.lookupObjects), the navigation property is read from the relationship metadata, and the write is a webAPI.updateRecord with @odata.bind followed by a refresh. Clear empties the cell the same way. The dialog is the demo's own searchable list rather than the platform's, with its views; media/screenshot-lookup.png is the real one, captured from the dev rig in this repository.

presets.name: Default
presets.description: An eight-column, 24-row view with sortable columns, a per-column filter row and multi-row selection.

presets.name: Grouped with totals
presets.description: Five owners, largest first, each with its record count and the revenue summed beneath it. Collapsed, the group list is the whole table — no member rows until you open one. Opening one is a filter, which this harness cannot apply; see the limitations.

presets.name: Pinned columns
presets.description: Account name held at the start and Modified on at the end while the six between them scroll behind. Drag the scrollbar under the rows, then try the phone preview: the control unpins itself when the pair would leave nothing to scroll.

presets.name: Inline editing
presets.description: Click any cell to edit it in place — Primary contact opens a lookup over the demo's contacts. Account number is marked read-only in the fixture, so it stays plain text: the control asks the platform which cells are writable. New opens a quick create.

presets.name: Filtering and export
presets.description: The filter row with a rows-per-page picker and CSV export, showing which column types get a box — text, number, and since 0.4.0 a date picker with an On / From / Until chip — and which do not. Export CSV's file is offered as a download in the event log.
